content: Leading-wildcard LIKE percent-term-percent cannot use a B-tree index and full-text search is the wrong tool for serial codes because it tokenizes whole stemmed words, not substrings. The standard Postgres fix is pg_trgm GIN index which supports LIKE with leading wildcards; constraints: pattern needs at least 3 characters to produce trigrams, GIN is read-optimized and slow to build (fine for mostly-static serial data). Official pg_trgm docs plus Stack Overflow, pgAnalyze, SQLPerformance corroborate. At asset-tracker scale (hundreds to low thousands of rows) a plain LIKE scan is actually fine, making premature index optimization a lesser risk than missing normalization of serial formats.
